SMTO-SCH-0030 — The Agent couldn't reach SMTO's saved schedules

GUID: d5bd8f28-d927-47df-b589-cbc1d5379d59
Slug: schedule-store-unavailable
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: sch

What happened

  • The Agent tried to create, view or change a schedule, but the place SMTO keeps schedules wasn't available to it. No schedule was created or changed by this step.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Schedules. If it shows Schedules unavailable or won't load, restart SMTO the way you normally do and wait for Ready. SMTO connects to its saved schedules when it starts, so a clean start usually fixes this.
  2. Once the Schedules page loads, look for the schedule you asked about to see its current state. This shows whether anything needs doing before you ask again.
  3. Then ask the Agent again in the conversation, or make the change yourself with New schedule or Edit. With saved schedules reachable again, the same request can go through.

What success looks like

  • The Schedules page lists your schedules, and the Agent's schedule step finishes without an error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who installed SMTO. Don't delete SMTO's data folder; it holds your saved schedules.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The native Schedule capability ran without an event_store in its execution context, so no schedule operation could be performed.

What this means

  • The native schedule capability receives no event_store in its execution context. Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.

Why this can happen

  • The native schedule capability receives no event_store in its execution context.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect Controller service initialization and captured context before changing schedule arguments.

How to fix it

  • NativeScheduleCapability.execute found execution_context.event_store missing; it is normally supplied to Agent runs by the Server when the events services start. Check the Server log for event-store or schedule-service startup failures, restart the Server through the supported startup, and confirm the Schedules page loads before retrying.
  • Restore the supported schedule-store configuration on the controller before creating durable scheduled work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported schedule store is available to the intended operation.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
